English construction: Concessive clause
Example: “Although the lantern was dim, we found the trail.”
The subordinate clause grants a circumstance that might have suggested the opposite result.

English construction: Purpose clause
Example: “I marked the jar so that nobody would mistake its contents for sugar.”
So that introduces the intended purpose of the action.

English construction: Result construction
Example: “The current was so strong that we turned back.”
So plus adjective pairs with a that-clause expressing the consequence.

English construction: Absolute construction
Example: “The tide having turned, we lowered the boat.”
The participial clause has its own expressed subject and provides circumstances for the main clause.
